content:
- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.27) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–2% of recent mean or 0.5–1.0 price point.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.27), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–2% or 0.5–1.0 price point.
- Model consistently under-estimates price spikes in the 10–15 day horizon; add 0.5–1.5 price point buffer after a spike.
- Model over-estimates 30-day averages when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5 price point for 30d horizon.
- Model shows lag in reacting to sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns positive after 3–5 days, adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead by +0.5–1.0 price point.
- For 30d forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model often fails to capture mean reversion; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 price point in the 20–30 day range.
